facts.expectation: No prescribed report format or pro-forma; the report should be factual and establish inherently low risk.
The report should clarify that it informs the building fire risk assessment (FRA) in the Fire Safety Order context.
The report should not claim compliance with building regulations, either currently or when constructed.

Where the building or all relevant external walls are determined inherently low risk under Clause 4 by following the Figure 1 process, the report should include a statement of the signatories' competence to make that determination.
The report should identify the appraiser's name and organisation.
The report should give its completion date and the building inspection date(s).
The report should give the building address.
The report should identify the building use or uses.
The report should give the building dimensions.
The report should state the building's approximate age.
The report should explain how inherently low risk was established.
The report should provide information to assist dutyholders with applicable statutory obligations.
Preserve the distinction between SHOULD and MUST, conditional scope, and the separation between fire-risk information and building-regulation compliance.
